about: Should you put a wet phone in rice. Factory #40, backlog row 45, slug rice. One hard idea: Apple's own support page ('If you see a liquid-detection alert on your iPhone', Oct 30, 2024) says 'Don't put your iPhone in a bag of rice. Doing so could allow small particles of rice to damage your iPhone', on the same list as heat, compressed air and cotton swabs; charging while the connector is wet can corrode the pins; instead tap it gently against your hand with the connector down, leave it in a dry area with some airflow, and it might take up to 24 hours to fully dry; check yours: try charging later, and the liquid alert (iPhone XS, XR or later) means it's still wet. Sources read 2026-11-23, see BRIEF.md.
